name: Edge hardened baseline
description: This project's opinion of a reasonable baseline for an unattended Linux edge device: a mandatory access control system enforcing, appraised file integrity, a read-only verified root, a locked-down kernel, and the common kernel self-protection options. It is a baseline, not a certification. A FAIL here means the device does not match this opinion; whether that matters depends on the device's threat model.

checks.title: SELinux is enforcing
checks.why: Permissive mode logs denials but does not prevent them.

checks.title: IMA appraisal is enforcing
checks.why: With appraisal off or in log mode, unsigned or modified files still execute.

checks.title: Root filesystem is on device-mapper
checks.why: A root on a raw partition has no integrity protection below the filesystem.

checks.title: A device-mapper target is active
checks.why: No active mapper target means no dm-verity or dm-crypt in the boot chain.

checks.title: Kernel lockdown is integrity or confidentiality
checks.why: Without lockdown, root can replace the running kernel through kexec, /dev/mem or unsigned modules.

checks.title: Kernel text and rodata are write-protected
Module text and rodata are write-protected
Memory zeroed on allocation by default
